name: Rewind Review Sync for Google Maps and Elementor
author: jakirulislambd19

sections.description:
Rewind Review Sync for Google Maps and Elementor pulls real Google Maps reviews into WordPress and stores each one as a post. From there you can display them two ways: with the bundled Google Reviews widget (works with free Elementor), or by building your own Loop Grid template using the plugin’s dynamic tags (requires Elementor Pro).

Reviews are fetched through the Apify platform, an external third-party service you connect with your own account. See the “External services” section below for exactly what is sent and when.

Key features

  • Automatic sync — reviews refresh on a configurable schedule using WordPress Cron (default: every 24 hours)
  • Manual sync — trigger a fresh fetch at any time from the plugin’s admin screen
  • Design gallery and shortcode — preview ready-made layouts (sliders, grids, badges, popups and more) in the admin screen and place one anywhere with [rewind_reviews design="slider-header-shadow"]
  • Bundled Elementor widget — slider, grid and list layouts with full style controls, no Elementor Pro required
  • Loop Grid ready — every review field is available as an Elementor dynamic tag for your own templates
  • Place-level data — the overall average rating and total review count are stored and available as tags
  • No bundled libraries — built entirely on the WordPress HTTP API, WP-Cron and native Elementor APIs

Available dynamic tags

All tags appear under the Google Reviews group in the Elementor dynamic tags picker:

  • Review Rating (1-5) — text and number categories
  • Reviewer Photo — image category
  • Review Date — text category, relative or formatted
  • Reviewer Profile URL — text and URL categories
  • Place Average Rating — text and number categories
  • Total Review Count — text and number categories

The reviewer’s name and the review body are stored as the post title and post content, so use Elementor’s built-in Post Title and Post Content dynamic tags for those.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.5 or later
  • PHP 7.4 or later
  • Elementor 3.5 or later for the review widget
  • Elementor Pro for Loop Grid and dynamic tags
  • A free Apify account

Elementor is a hard requirement and is declared through the Requires Plugins header, so WordPress will not activate this plugin until Elementor is installed and active.

How it works

  1. Reviews are fetched from Google Maps by running the compass~google-maps-reviews-scraper actor on Apify
  2. Each review is saved as a post of the rewind_review custom post type
  3. Review metadata (rating, photo, date, profile URL) is stored in post meta
  4. Place-level data (average rating, total count) is stored as a site option
  5. Everything is exposed to Elementor as a widget and as dynamic tags

External services

This plugin connects to the services below. Apify is required for syncing reviews. Freemius is optional and only starts after you agree to it. Google image servers are contacted by your visitors’ browsers when reviewer photos are shown.

Apify (required for syncing reviews)

This plugin relies on the Apify platform (https://apify.com) to retrieve Google Maps reviews. It does not work without it.

What the service is used for: running the Google Maps Reviews Scraper actor, which collects the public reviews for the business URL you configure and returns them to your site.

What data is sent, and when: the Google Maps URL you enter in the plugin settings, and your Apify API token for authentication. The scraper is asked to include reviewer details, so each review is saved with the reviewer’s public name, profile photo address and profile link as well as the rating, text and date. This is public Google Maps information. Data is sent only when you click Sync Now, or when the scheduled automatic sync runs. No request is made until you have entered your own Apify token and saved it.

Where the data goes: https://api.apify.com/

  • Apify Terms of Service: https://docs.apify.com/legal/general-terms-and-conditions
  • Apify Privacy Policy: https://docs.apify.com/legal/privacy-policy

Freemius (optional usage insights)

This plugin includes the Freemius SDK (https://freemius.com) to learn how the plugin is used so it can be improved. Every feature of the plugin is free and works whether or not you opt in.

What happens by default: nothing is sent. After activation an opt-in screen asks whether you want to share information. Choose Skip and no data is sent to Freemius.

What data is sent if you opt in: your WordPress user’s name and email address, your site’s URL and title, the WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, the site language, and the list of installed plugins and themes with their versions. Freemius may also receive basic events such as activation, deactivation and uninstall. You can opt out at any time from Google Reviews → Account, which stops further data being sent.

Where the data goes: https://api.freemius.com/

  • Freemius Terms of Service: https://freemius.com/terms/
  • Freemius Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Google image servers (reviewer photos)

Reviews show the reviewer’s profile photo. The photo address is stored on your site as part of each review, and the image itself is loaded by the visitor’s browser directly from Google’s image servers (for example lh3.googleusercontent.com). As with any image hosted elsewhere, this means the visitor’s IP address and browser details are visible to Google when a photo loads. The plugin asks the browser not to send a referrer. Your site does not send any visitor data to Google itself.

  • Google Terms of Service: https://policies.google.com/terms
  • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Source code and third-party assets

The admin screen is a React app. The compiled file assets/admin.js and the stylesheets in assets/css/ are built from the readable sources shipped in this plugin’s source/ folder (TypeScript, React and Sass), together with package.json, webpack.config.js and the other build files. To rebuild, run npm install and then npm run build in the plugin folder.

The plugin bundles the Freemius SDK in the freemius/ folder, licensed under GPLv3.

The admin screen is built with React and bundles these open-source libraries (all MIT licensed): Redux Toolkit and React Redux, React Router, and clsx. It also uses the React and i18n packages that WordPress itself provides. The Google logo shown in some layouts is a trademark of Google LLC and is used only to identify reviews that come from Google.

The admin screen bundles the Poppins font, which is licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. It is served from the plugin folder; no fonts, scripts or styles are loaded from an external server.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the rewind-review-sync-for-google-maps folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress
  3. Go to Google Reviews → Settings
  4. Enter your Google Maps URL — open the business in Google Maps on desktop and copy the full URL from the address bar
  5. Enter your Apify API Token — find it at https://console.apify.com under Account → Integrations
  6. Click Save Settings, then click Sync Now
  7. In Elementor, either drop in the Google Reviews widget, or add a Loop Grid, set its query post type to Google Review, and build your template with the Google Reviews dynamic tags
sections.faq:
Do I need a paid Apify account?

No. Apify’s free tier includes monthly credit and does not require a credit card. For most sites a daily sync stays comfortably within it.

How do I get my Google Maps URL?

Open Google Maps on desktop, search for the business, and copy the full URL from the browser address bar. It looks like https://www.google.com/maps/place/Business+Name/....

Where do I find my Apify API token?

Log in at https://console.apify.com, go to Account → Integrations, and copy your personal API token.

How often does the plugin sync?

Every 24 hours by default, via WordPress Cron. Change it under Google Reviews → Settings → Auto-Sync Interval, with a minimum of one hour. You can also sync manually at any time with the Sync Now button.

Can I use this without Elementor Pro?

Yes. The bundled Google Reviews widget works with the free version of Elementor. Loop Grid and dynamic tags are Elementor Pro features, so those parts require Pro.

Do I need Elementor at all?

Yes. Elementor is declared as a dependency, so WordPress will not let you activate this plugin without it. Once synced, the reviews are stored as ordinary posts, so any theme or plugin can also read them.

The average rating or review count shows 0. Why?

These come from the place-level fields in the Apify response for each sync. Click Sync Now to refresh. If they stay at 0, the actor’s response may not include place-level fields for your particular URL.

What happens to existing reviews when I sync again?

They are updated in place, matched on the Google review ID. No duplicates are created.

Does the plugin collect any data about me?

Only if you choose to. On activation a Freemius opt-in screen asks whether to share basic usage information. Choosing Skip sends nothing. See External services above for exactly what is sent.

Will the plugin ask me for a review?

Once, on the plugin’s own admin screen only, after the plugin has been active for seven days, and only for administrators. You can leave a review, choose Maybe later (it will not reappear for 14 days) or choose No thanks to hide it permanently. Nothing is offered in return for a review, and the plugin never posts a review for you.

What is removed when I delete the plugin?

Deleting the plugin removes its settings, its scheduled sync, and the synced review posts. Those reviews are a cache of data held by Google rather than content you authored, and reinstalling plus running one sync restores them.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: Designs gallery in the admin screen with live previews of ready-made review layouts
  • New: [rewind_reviews] shortcode so reviews can be placed in any post, page, template or widget area
  • New: Elementor widget layouts: header sliders, masonry, compact list, rating badge, rating button, floating badge, sidebar and FOMO notification
  • New: “Load more” for review lists, served from a signed REST route
  • New: A dismissible request for a WordPress.org review on the plugin’s own screen after seven days
  • New: Optional Freemius opt-in for usage insights. Nothing is sent unless you agree, and every feature stays free
  • Improved: Redesigned admin screen
  • Security: The Apify token is no longer sent to the browser, is not autoloaded and is kept when the field is left blank
  • Security: Reviews have no public page, search result or REST route, and only administrators can edit them
  • Security: Review text is stored as plain text; the settings form validates the Google Maps URL and actor ID
  • Security: Design previews run in a sandboxed frame without access to the admin page
  • Fixed: Reviews moved to the trash are no longer restored by the next sync
  • Fixed: Reviews with no rating are no longer counted as five stars, and the header word (Excellent, Great, Good) follows the score
  • Improved: Sync Now runs in the background and the Overview screen shows its progress, so slow Apify runs no longer time out the request
  • Improved: Syncing many reviews is faster
  • Fixed: A manual and a scheduled sync can no longer run at the same time
  • Security: The signed “load more” links expire (30 days by default, adjustable with the rewind_load_signature_ttl filter)
  • Changed: The “Verified Google Review” badge is now labelled “Review from Google”
  • Improved: Existing Elementor widgets keep their saved layout and styling
  • Improved: Settings and sync data from 1.0.0 are upgraded automatically on update
  • Fixed: Other plugins’ admin notices are no longer hidden on the plugin screen

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • rewind_review custom post type synced from Apify
  • Google Reviews Elementor widget with slider, grid and list layouts
  • Six Elementor dynamic tags: Review Rating, Reviewer Photo, Review Date, Reviewer Profile URL, Place Average Rating, Total Review Count
  • Configurable auto-sync interval via WordPress Cron, plus a manual sync button
